# 1 Enoch Chapter 73 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** After this I was shown a second law — the law governing the lesser light, the Moon.

**2** The moon travels on the same great circuit as the heavens. In the darkness, her chariot is carried by the wind, and she receives her light in carefully measured amounts.

**3** Each month, as she sets out and returns, her brightness is not constant — her light varies at different points in her circuit.

**4** In the first month, she rises in the greater light. At her appointed time she rises together with the sun through the same gate, and catches just a sliver of sunlight — half of one-seventh — so that her visible disc shows one-and-a-half sevenths illuminated.

**5** She sets with the sun. When the sun rises again, she rises with it, picking up half a unit of light. On the first night of the lunar month, when the new day begins, she sets with the sun and is completely invisible — her disc holding fourteen-and-a-half parts of darkness.

**6** The next day she rises with exactly one-seventh part lit, pulling away from the sun; and over the remaining days she grows steadily brighter, gaining light across the remaining thirteen parts.

**7** I was shown this further course and law by which the moon completes her monthly circuit.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. The 14-part phase system tracks the moon's waxing and waning with one part added or removed per night. The moon is fundamentally the lesser light — she receives rather than generates light, reinforcing the hierarchical cosmology of the Astronomical Book.*
